newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK OF CENTRAL GREECE STAFF TO STRIKE JULY 14.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF CENTRAL GREECE STAFF TO STRIKE JULY 14.

text.p: Staff of the Bank of Central Greece said in a statement they will strike on Monday July 14 to protest against the planned sale of the bank by parent Agricultural Bank to private Egnatia Bank.

"The strike aims to stop the tender which in our opinion would amount to a selloff of the bank," the statement said, noting that the Egnatia Bank's bid -- the only one -- was rejected by the evaluation committee because it was too low.
On July 4 Agricultural Bank called on Egnatia to begin negotiations for the sale of its majority stake in the Bank of Central Greece which has 22 branches and 500 employees.
Egnatia was the only bank out of six to express interest in the early stage of the tender to submit a binding bid.
The six Greek and foreign banks that showed interest in the tender were: Bank of Nova Scotia, Egnatia Bank, Hellenic Bank of Cyprus, Eurobank, Aspis Group and Piraeus Bank.
Agricultural Bank holds 56 percent of common registered shares and 21 percent of preferred shares in the Bank of Central Greece which was founded in 1936 and listed on the Athens bourse in 1991.
